newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. agency shows skeletal North Korean children.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency shows skeletal North Korean children.

text.p: Starving children in North Korea have been reduced to pitiful, skeletal figures too weak even to eat the emergency rations that are being sent by the West, the U.N.'s food aid agency said on Tuesday.

The Rome-based World Food Programme released film footage shot last week during visits to hospitals and nurseries showing some of the most dramatic images to date of the effects of the country's worsening food crisis.

The footage, distributed to media organisations, shows one emaciated child, aged around five, lying close to death on a bed in a paediatric hospital in Hamhung, South Hamgyon Province, on North Korea's east coast.
A four-year-old farmer's son from Sinsong Ri, one of the towns worst hit in two years of devastating floods, lies on a hospital bed in North Hwanghae Province, southeast of Pyongyang.
The boy, Kim Chong-ill, has lost almost all of his subcutaneous fat and each rib is clearly visible beneath the tightly stretched skin.

One girl, aged three, weighs just 10 kg (22 lbs) and has badly infected skin sores. Other children have developed the bowed legs characteristic of vitamin deficiency and have swollen joints and protruding stomachs.

"The situation in North Korea is getting worse and we are seeing children who are just skin and bone, who have had nothing to eat and who cannot even consume the ground-up corn that we have available for them," WFP Executive Director Catherine Bertini said.
"We are having to find increased amounts of special baby food that is highly nutritious to be able to feed malnourished children."
WFP quoted Choi Jung-bu, principal of the General Hospital of Kusong City, southeast of Pyongyang, as saying his hospital had turned away malnutrition cases for lack of food.
Bertini said doctors were concentrating on patients who were both malnourished and suffering from serious diseases.
"There is no question that the World Food Programme will be increasing its appeal to donors for food for these hungry children and we will move the food there as quickly as possible," she said.
